note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is never pictured: where Job speaks to God, God's side is an empty judge's bench, an empty chair or a drawn curtain. Job and his friends are not portrayed as biblical people but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown. Verse 15 follows the main text ("he will kill me; I will not wait; but I will argue my ways to his face"), so its picture shows the bold walk to the bench, not trust in waiting.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: Job knows as much as his friends; he turns from their lies smeared over his wound and their worthless cures to bring his case to God himself, and their silence would be their wisdom.
ideas: Three men talk at a tired man at a kitchen table all at once, while he turns his face away and up toward a bright window
A man stands on a hillside with his back to three men still arguing below him, looking up into the open sky
A trowel smooths fresh plaster over a deep crack in a wall, and the crack runs on past both ends of the patch
A small sticking plaster stuck across a wide crack in a concrete wall
A man walks out of a room of arguing men through an open doorway into daylight
A doctor hands a man with his arm in a sling a single sugar cube
A man sits writing a letter by lamplight, ignoring the voices from the next room
A man pushes away a pile of advice notes heaped in front of him
A friend sits silently beside a grieving man, saying nothing
A man covers his ears while three people talk at him

sections.meaning: Speaking lies to defend God is itself wrong: God sees through it and will correct them, and their sayings are as worthless as ashes and as weak as clay.
ideas: A man speaks earnestly with his hand on his heart while behind his back his other hand has its fingers crossed
A man speaks to an audience holding a smiling mask on a stick in front of his face
A garden wall of unfired clay bricks slumps and crumbles in the rain
Burnt pages in a cold fireplace keep their shape as grey ash and fall apart as the air lifts them
A flashlight beam picks out a man hiding something behind his back in a dark room
An airport scanner screen shows everything hidden inside a suitcase
A man bows far too low before a grand empty chair
Ash runs out of an open hand and blows away in the wind
A shield made of dried clay cracks in two
A sandcastle wall dissolving as the tide comes in

sections.meaning: Come what may, Job will risk his life to argue his ways to God's face, sure that he will be found in the right, since a godless man would never dare to come before him.
ideas: A lone man walks up the centre aisle of a vast empty courtroom toward the high empty judge's bench, a folder of papers in his hand
A man steps out of a sheltered doorway into a fierce storm and walks into it upright
A man stands at the table in an empty courtroom facing the high bench, his papers laid out in front of him, head high
Late at night at a kitchen table a man has laid out his papers in neat rows, sitting upright and calm
A man walks across a narrow plank over a deep gorge
A man holds a small flame cupped in his hands in the wind
A man climbs alone up a steep mountain path toward a summit in cloud
A man stands still on the shore facing a great wave rolling in
A man signs his name at the foot of a long statement and puts down the pen
A man knocks on the tall closed doors of a great hall

sections.meaning: Job asks only that the crushing hand and the terror be taken away, so that he and God can truly speak: God calls and he answers, or he speaks and God replies.
ideas: A man sits leaning forward on a chair, hands open, speaking to an empty chair facing him
A man on a hilltop at evening cups his hands round his mouth and calls across a wide valley
A man waits beside a phone, ready to pick it up the moment it rings
A heavy weight is lifted off a man's shoulders and he straightens up
A man steps out from behind a wall into open light, ready to be seen
A radio operator in headphones leans in, listening for a reply
Two chairs drawn up face to face at a small table in a quiet room
A man stands at a lectern in an empty hall, waiting for a question
A man crouching under a dark shadow straightens as the shadow lifts
A man raises his hand to speak in a hushed meeting room

sections.meaning: Job asks to be told his wrongs and why God hides his face and treats him as an enemy, hounding a frail man like a blown leaf and watching his every step while he wears away like a moth-eaten garment.
ideas: At dusk a man stands outside a house looking up at a lit window whose curtain has just been drawn shut
A man stands at the gate of a house with every curtain drawn
A single dry leaf is driven along an empty country road by the wind
A dry leaf is chased across a harvested field of stubble by a gust
A man's ankle fitted with an electronic monitor, its small light glowing
A man walks along a path while security cameras on poles turn to follow him
An old wool coat on a hook, eaten through with moth holes
A moth-eaten jacket on a chair by a window, light shining through its holes

candidates.prompt: In a plain kitchen in daylight, three middle-aged men stand round a tired grey-haired man who sits at the table. All three are talking at him at once: one wags a finger, one counts points on his fingers, one leans over him with folded arms. The seated man is not listening to them: he has turned his face away from them and up toward a tall bright window, looking out at the open sky, as if he would rather speak to someone higher.

Close view of a plain interior wall split by a long, deep, jagged crack that runs right across it. A man's hand holding a plasterer's trowel is smoothing a neat patch of fresh white plaster over the middle of the crack, but the deep crack plainly carries on out of both ends of the fresh patch, as wide as ever. Even daylight from the side.

Close view of a thick grey concrete wall with a wide, deep crack running right across it. Stuck across the middle of the crack is one small, ordinary beige adhesive bandage, the kind put on a scratched finger, looking absurdly tiny against the deep crack, which carries on past it on both sides. Even daylight.

Seen from behind and a little to one side, a man in a suit stands in a plain hall speaking earnestly to a small seated audience, one hand pressed to his heart. His other hand is held behind his back at the small of his back, and its first two fingers are crossed, the sign of telling a lie. The crossed fingers are sharp and clear in the middle of the frame; the audience is soft in the background.

In a plain hall, a man in a suit stands speaking to a small seated audience. In one hand he holds a smiling white mask on a stick in front of his own face, so that the audience sees only the fixed smile. Seen from the side, so his real face behind the mask is visible to us: tense and unsmiling. Soft daylight.

In steady rain, a garden wall built of unfired clay bricks is slumping and crumbling into mud: a wide breach has opened in the middle where the bricks have melted and fallen in a heap, and brown water runs down the rest of the wall. Grey overcast light.

In a cold stone fireplace lies a stack of burnt pages that has turned entirely to grey ash but still keeps the shape of the pages. A breath of air from the room is lifting the top sheets of ash and they are crumbling and drifting apart into flakes. Plain soft daylight from a window. The pages are blank grey ash with no writing visible.

Seen from behind, a lone man in plain everyday clothes walks up the centre aisle of a vast, empty, wood-panelled courtroom toward the judge's bench, which stands high and empty at the far end with an empty chair behind it. He holds a folder of papers at his side and his shoulders are squared. Tall windows let in clear light that falls on the empty bench. The rows of seats on either side are empty.

A man in a plain coat steps out of the shelter of a doorway straight into a fierce storm, rain driving sideways and his coat whipping in the wind. He walks forward into it with his head up and his face set, not turning back. Grey stormy daylight.

In a vast, empty, wood-panelled courtroom, a man in plain everyday clothes stands alone at the table in front of the high empty judge's bench, his papers laid out in neat order on the table before him. He stands upright with his head high and calm, facing the empty bench, ready to be heard. Clear light from tall windows falls on him.

In a vast, empty, wood-panelled courtroom with plain panelled walls, a man in plain everyday clothes stands alone at the table in front of the high empty judge's bench, his papers laid out in neat order on the table before him. He stands upright with his head high and calm, facing the empty bench, ready to be heard. Clear light from tall windows falls on him. No flags, no seals, no emblems or plaques anywhere in the room.

Late at night at a plain kitchen table under a single warm lamp, a grey-haired man sits upright and calm. In front of him he has laid out his papers in neat, ordered rows across the table, every sheet squared, and his hands rest flat on the table beside them. His face is quiet and sure. The pages show no readable writing.

In a quiet bare room with soft window light, a man sits on a plain wooden chair leaning forward, his hands open, speaking, his face earnest. Facing him, a few steps away, stands a second plain wooden chair, empty, turned toward him, as if waiting for the other side of the conversation.

On a grassy hilltop at evening, a man stands with his hands cupped round his mouth, calling out across a wide, empty valley toward the far hills. His body leans forward and his whole stance is waiting for an answer to come back. Soft clear evening light, not a sunset.

At dusk, a man stands alone in the garden of a house, looking up at a lit upstairs window. The curtain of that window has just been drawn shut, so only a thin line of light shows at its edge. His hand is half raised toward the window and his face asks why. The rest of the house is dark.

In evening light, a man stands at the front gate of a quiet house. Every window of the house has its curtains drawn shut, and the front door is closed. He stands looking up at the closed windows, his arms at his sides, a pleading question in his face.

A single dry brown leaf is being driven along an empty country road by a strong wind, tumbling in the air just above the road. Beside the road lies a harvested field of dry pale stubble. A wide grey windy sky.

Low close view across a harvested field of dry, pale stubble: one single dry brown leaf is being chased across the stubble by a gust of wind, lifted and tumbling, with a few loose bits of straw blowing after it. Pale, windy daylight.

Close view of a man sitting on the edge of a bed, his trouser leg pulled up: strapped round his bare ankle is a black electronic ankle monitor with a small glowing light. The ankle and the monitor are in the middle of the frame, large and sharp, at eye level; the plain bedroom floor is below.

A man walks alone along a path through an empty park. On tall poles on both sides of the path, several security cameras are all turned toward him, following him as he walks. He glances up at them. Flat grey daylight.

An old wool coat hangs alone on a hook against a plain wall, worn thin and eaten through with many moth holes, its hem frayed. Soft side light shows the holes clearly. A single small moth rests on the shoulder.

An old wool jacket is laid over the back of a wooden chair beside a window. It has been eaten through with moth holes, and bright window light shines through the many holes. A single small moth rests on the collar.
